plan.topic: An itchy rash or itchy patch of skin away from the injection spot on tirzepatide: what the US label says about hypersensitivity reactions vs placebo, and which signs mean emergency care
plan.angle:
Keep the 08:00 'Is this normal?' set-up, the tight arm (90–120 words, exact count logged), the mix at masking 0.02 or lower, no skin close-ups, no subscribe or link line, and the Exp G post note: the target is the Side Effects long video.
Sentence 1, with matching on-screen text: 'Itchy rash on tirzepatide? The label says most allergic-type reactions in trials were skin reactions.' Spoken, 'most' stands in for the label's 'the majority', which is the label's own claim, not one we're adding. Do not say 'most weren't serious'.
By 6 s, show one stat copied from Zepbound PI section 6.1, using the non-immediate figure only. Spoken: 'about three and a half in a hundred on tirzepatide versus about three in a hundred on placebo had reactions that started after the first day.' Card: '3.5% VS 2.7% PLACEBO · NON-IMMEDIATE HYPERSENSITIVITY REACTIONS · ZEPBOUND LABEL, STUDIES 1 AND 2: ADULTS WITH OBESITY, OR OVERWEIGHT PLUS A WEIGHT-RELATED CONDITION (STUDY 2: TYPE 2 DIABETES ONLY), UP TO 72 WEEKS'. Optional second line, if the word count allows: 'Severe reactions: 0.1% vs none on placebo (section 5.6).' Never add the two types together or write '5 vs 3'.
Cite only the Zepbound label (DailyMed updated 16 Nov 2026; PI 'Revised: 11/2026') and the separate Zepbound Medication Guide URL with its own 'Revised: 11/2026' date. Never use Mounjaro's date. Don't say what causes it, and keep it separate from injection-site reactions.
Replace the untagged line with: 'A new rash or itching is a reason to contact your prescriber promptly.'
Next, the emergency card: the Medication Guide's allergy list copied word for word after checking it against the guide PDF, followed by its 'stop using … and get medical help right away' wording. 'Or call your local emergency number' is our own line and gets no tag.
Do not use the standard don't-stop line here, because the label advises stopping and seeking medical attention if a hypersensitivity reaction occurs. Use instead: 'If it is only a mild rash or itch, call your prescriber before your next dose, and let them decide whether you keep going.' Make it one clause per card and do not run it through the auto-splitter.
Then 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.' and the loop line back to sentence 1. No digits or contractions in the narration outside the fixed lines, and no 'now' or 'new'.
The title can stay as 'Tirzepatide Itchy Rash: Allergy or Normal? #shorts', or use the safer 'Tirzepatide and Itchy Rash: What the Label Says #shorts'.
plan.working_title: Tirzepatide Itchy Rash: Allergy or Normal? #shorts
plan.why:
Replaces the held 08:00 hair Short with another proven 'Is this normal?' visible body moment. Every fact comes from one label section and its Medication Guide, so it should pass the fact-check first time. No other piece today covers skin or allergy. | fact-check: The topic is fine: it's a real, evergreen question, it's on-label, and it helps keep viewers safe. But I checked the current Zepbound label on DailyMed (Revised 11/2026, DailyMed updated 16 Nov 2026, setid 487cd7e7-434c-4925-99fa-aa80b1cc776b), and three parts of the brief don't match it.
(1) The planned stat '5 in 100 vs 3 in 100' is not in section 6.1. The label splits reactions into two types and gives no combined figure: 'immediate hypersensitivity reactions (within one day after drug administration) occurred in 2.1% of ZEPBOUND-treated patients compared to 0.4% of placebo-treated patients, while non-immediate hypersensitivity reactions occurred in 3.5% … compared to 2.7%'. Adding the two together ourselves would be our own arithmetic presented as the label's number.
(2) The label never says 'most weren't serious'. Its words are: 'The majority of the hypersensitivity reactions in trials were skin reactions (e.g., rash, itching).' Section 5.6 adds that severe reactions occurred in 0.1% on Zepbound vs no one on placebo, and that serious reactions (anaphylaxis, angioedema) were seen in postmarketing reports.
(3) This is a safety conflict. Section 5.6 says: 'If hypersensitivity reactions occur, advise patients to promptly seek medical attention and discontinue use of ZEPBOUND.' Following a rash Short with the standard 'don't stop or change your medicine on your own' line could be read as 'keep injecting through an allergic reaction', which goes against the label. The mild 'worth telling your prescriber' line also understates the label's 'promptly'.
Two smaller points. The pool is Studies 1 and 2, so the card should name both: Study 1 had no type 2 diabetes, Study 2 had type 2 diabetes only. I could not read the Medication Guide text through the tool, so the allergy list in the brief is not confirmed and must be checked against the Medication Guide PDF (Revised 11/2026). 'Or call your local emergency number' is our own line and gets no source tag. The working title is acceptable, but 'Normal?' should not suggest that a rash is expected.

script.cta: POST NOTES. Revision fixes from the fact-checker: (1) the s3 stat attribution is now 'ZEPBOUND LABEL, SECTION 5.6: ZEPBOUND CLINICAL STUDIES'; (2) s5 list item 7 is now exactly 'OR CALL YOUR LOCAL EMERGENCY NUMBER.' and the 'our own line, no source tag' note has moved to the visual fact field. Nothing else has changed. Length arm: standard. The angle text says "tight", but the task sets standard (135–160 words), so I followed the task. Exact spoken word count, counted by hand: 157 (s1 17, s2 26, s3 15, s4 13, s5 50, s6 24, s7 12). Exp G watch-next target: the Side Effects long video. The publisher adds the verified link and the copywriter leaves line 1 empty. Title: the safer 'Tirzepatide and Itchy Rash: What the Label Says #shorts', so we don't suggest a rash is expected. Production: masking 0.02 or lower on the final file (aim for 0.015); no skin close-ups; no subscribe or 'link in the description' line or card. Speech-to-text check: 'tirzepatide' in s1, s2 and s3. The safety cards in s5, s6 and s7 are pre-split; never run them through the auto-splitter. Facts: only the Zepbound label (Revised 11/2026; DailyMed updated 16 Nov 2026) and the separate Zepbound Medication Guide (Revised 11/2026). Mounjaro's date is not used. The immediate and non-immediate figures are never added together. Spoken, the label's 'the majority' stays as 'the majority'. No claim about cause, and nothing about injection-site reactions. Before render: check the s5 allergy list word for word against the Medication Guide PDF, and confirm the guide's own 'Revised: 11/2026' date on the PDF. Our own lines (s4, 'Or call your local emergency number', s6, s7) carry no source tag. The standard don't-stop line is deliberately left out, as the angle asked.

factcheck.summary:
This Short passes, with two small fixes listed below. I checked it against the live Zepbound label on DailyMed: printed "Revised: 11/2026", DailyMed updated 16 Nov 2026. Every number in it is in the label.

**Checked against section 6.1 (pooled Studies 1 and 2):**
- The label's "majority" wording appears there word for word: "The majority of the hypersensitivity reactions in trials were skin reactions (e.g., rash, itching)."
- The non-immediate figure is 3.5% on Zepbound vs 2.7% on placebo. The label defines immediate as "within one day after drug administration", so "started after the first day" is accurate. The immediate figure (2.1% vs 0.4%) is correctly kept separate.

**Checked against section 5.6:** severe reactions were 0.1% vs none on placebo. The label also tells patients to "promptly seek medical attention", which matches s4's "contact your prescriber promptly".

**Framing and safety:**
- There is no claim that the medicine causes the rash, and s2 shows the placebo rate next to the drug rate.
- s6 leaves the decision to the prescriber and gives no instruction to stop or keep going.
- The emergency list goes straight to medical help.

**Word count:** I recounted it by hand at 157 words, matching the post notes and inside the standard arm (135–160).

**Not fully checked:**
- I couldn't read the Medication Guide PDF's text with my tools. The s5 list matches the wording I know from the guide, and the post notes already require a word-for-word check against the PDF before render.
- I took the guide's "Revised: 11/2026" date from the brief's known-dates list, not from the PDF itself.
